newsitem.title: UK: Belfast punishment victim asks "Why me?".
newsitem.headline: Belfast punishment victim asks "Why me?".

text.p: His right leg reduced to a bruised stump, Sean McNally blamed an IRA "punishment squad" for his horrific wounds on Thursday and asked "Why me?".
Unemployed and a petty thief, he had the limb amputated above the knee last week after a three-man gang cornered him in a laneway and blasted his knee with a shotgun.
He stole car radios but never in his own area, he told reporters. The self-styled punishment gangs, whose usual weapons are nail-studded baseball bats and hammers, gave him no warning or reason.

Guerrilla vigilante squads have for decades exacted a terrifying toll in bitterly divided Northern Ireland's Protestant and Catholic enclaves, often "kneecapping", sometimes killing, suspected thieves, burglars and drug-peddlers.
The gang forced McNally, 24, to the ground, stood on his limbs and told him to keep his face to the ground.
"I felt somebody kicking my legs apart. That's when I felt the gun going off. I just started squealing. That's when I knew I was shot. I never felt pain like it before in my life," he said.
His days as a keen street footballer over, McNally has no doubts it was the Irish Republican Army, the chief guerrilla group engaged in a long-running armed campaign against British rule.
"The IRA, I know it was the IRA," he told a news conference, speaking from a wheel chair in Belfast's Royal Victoria Hospital.

"I would love to know why. Why me? People have done far worse things and have flesh wounds or a couple of broken bones, that's all they've got. For the sake of a couple of car radios, I got my leg blown off."

IRA sympathisers deny that the group did the shooting, according to media sources in Belfast. Pistols, not shotguns, are the IRA's stock in trade, say republicans who blame a smaller band of armed Catholic outlaws.
